lines.text: Today you choose your path and build a role kit of five prompts, each with the check that keeps it fair, accurate and safe.
Path A is HR, path B is an office administrator or executive assistant, and path C is a small business owner.
Every task today has an example for each path.
By the end you will have five prompts for your own role, each with its own check.
Ask the AI for a job post with the real duties, skills, hours and pay range.
Then run a bias check: remove age limits, gender, religion, marital status, looks, and words like young or native speaker.
Describe the skills the job needs, not the type of person.
Paste a public or approved policy section and ask for a plain-words version and a short list of common questions.
Check that no rule, number or date has changed.
The original policy always stays the official version.
AI can turn notes into formal minutes and draft the wording of a quotation or invoice.
Let your sheet or billing software do the maths, and never let the AI choose a tax rate.
Check every amount, tax detail and date before sending.
Never let AI shortlist, reject or rate candidates or staff on its own.
It can help you write fair questions, clear criteria and polite letters.
People make the decisions, and confidential HR data stays out of personal AI accounts.
An HR executive asks for a simple receptionist job post with the duties, hours and salary.
The AI copies old job-ad habits it has seen many times.
It adds an age limit, a gender, a pleasant personality and a photo, and none of that was asked for.
These lines shut out good candidates, so we run a bias check and rewrite the post around skills.
Now we ask Claude to check the same post for bias, and list every problem it finds.
It flags the age limit, the gender, the words about looks, and the photo request.
The rewrite describes the work and the skills, and welcomes freshers.
You still read the final version yourself, because the post goes out under your name.
A small business owner asks Copilot to draft a quotation with GST.
The layout and terms look professional and complete.
But the subtotal is wrong: forty times three fifty plus forty times one twenty is eighteen thousand, eight hundred.
So the AI writes the words, the sheet does the maths, and your accountant confirms the tax rate.
An office administrator turns meeting notes into formal minutes with owners and dates.
The AI should flag anything unclear, and you check every decision against your notes.
For policies, ask for plain words, then check that no rule or number changed.
Save each prompt with its check, so your kit is safe for a colleague to use too.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
